newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S&P upgrades Pioneer Intl to A-minus.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S&P upgrades Pioneer Intl to A-minus.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said on Monday it had upgraded its long term rating for Pioneer International Ltd to A-minus from BBB-plus.
S&P said the ratings outlook remained positive.
"The upgrade reflects Pioneer's improved operating cash flow stability derived from its effectively diversified aggregates and pre-mix concrete operations," S&P said.

The ratings agency said Pioneer's global spread of market leading construction materials businesses and its reasonably balanced exposure to both the residential and non-residential construction sectors reduce the company's reliance on any one market or sector.
"A significant decline in a major market, for example the new residential construction sector in Australia in fiscal 1996, does not significantly impair operating cash flow," it said.
"The upgrade recognises Standard and Poor's greater confidence that Pioneer's expansion strategy for the core construction materials business will be prudently managed," the ratings agency said.
It said Pioneer generated strong returns from its leading market positions in global pre-mixed concrete and aggregates businesses.

"While subject to cyclicality, Pioneer's operating cash flows benefit from well established, low cost operations, long term and well located aggregate reserves, and significant geographic and somewhat less end-market diversity," it said.
S&P said Pioneer would expand its offshore businesses significantly over the next three years.
"The company's focus will be on growth in aggregates, as well as concrete where integration with future or existing aggregate operations can be achieved," it said.
It said modest greenfields expansions were expected in Asia, especially India and Indonesia, while larger acquisitions were being sought in the United Kingdomg and United States.
"Pioneer has the debt capacity and strength in operating cash flows to fund an A$500 to A$600 million acquistion and greenfield expansions of A$750 million over the next three years," S&P said.
It said Pioneer's strategic growth ambitions would likely return total debt-to-capitalistion to the 30 percent to 40 percent range over the longer term.
"Failure to find suitable investment opportunities could result in a capital return to shareholders," the agency said.
S&P said Pioneer's 50 percent stake in petrol refiner and marketer Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd also provided cash flow diversity, although Pioneer was isolated from directly accessing AP's cashflow.

"Should Pioneer's substantial investment programme generate returns over the next three years consistent with its established operations, and further consolidate its global integrated building materials business, a rating upgrade may result," S&P said.
